paragraphs: Balancing Act sells simulation-based public engagement tools to government. The company describes an online simulation that draws stakeholders in so that leaders can make hard choices with public input behind them. The suite is aimed at budget, housing, climate and planning work.

In a budget simulation, residents see a model of the budget and their input is collected. A companion tool asks a few questions, estimates the taxes a household pays and shows where those dollars go. A mode for meetings turns the simulation into a facilitation tool for in-person and online sessions. There is also a research version for use with representative samples. The Prioritize product goes past a survey by having users pick items and then rank their picks. Its consensus analysis reports how many stakeholders end up with at least one of their choices included.

The housing product addresses cities and counties that struggle with public participation as they try to meet demand for new housing. Those simulations put residents in the shoes of decisionmakers and ask them to help solve the problem, with an interactive map showing where housing would be placed. Prioritize has been offered for input on stimulus funds such as ARPA and ESSER. A testimonial on the site is attributed to a village administrator in Germantown, Wisconsin.

quote.text: Balancing Act is an easy-to-use online simulation that engages stakeholders to help leaders make tough choices.
